scope: Engineering grip proxy applied as an explicit, logged external force channel. The frozen body XML is NOT modified. Any result obtained with this channel is labelled as a derived-channel result and is never reported as frozen-body acceptance.
why: Direction B showed that tarsal geometry cannot be folded into this body's joints, and that adhesion is a force channel rather than a joint angle. B3 tests whether grip is the binding constraint for planted-foot locomotion, using the smallest possible declared addition.

channel.name: grip
channel.applied_to: the tarsus body of each leg, as data.xfrc_applied force + moment at the contact point
channel.active_when: that leg has at least one tarsus-floor contact with normal load > 0.1 W
channel.force_law: F = -k_grip * v_tangential_at_contact, magnitude capped at F_max_per_leg; k_grip = 5000 native force units per native velocity unit, F_max_per_leg = 0.5 W
channel.update_rate: every 0.5 ms (every 40 native steps), the same cadence as the slip measurement
channel.logging: per update: active feet, per-leg applied force magnitude, cumulative impulse, plus the cap-hit count
channel.declared_bound_rationale: 0.5 W per leg puts the whole six-leg grip budget at 3 W, on the order of reported fly adhesion versus body weight; absolute SI is NOT_ESTABLISHED here so this is a declared engineering bound, not a calibrated adhesion value

unchanged: the frozen body XML and all of its hashes
gravity, timestep, solver, contact parameters, joint ranges, actuator gains and torque limits
the base network, the residual policy, the reward definition and the acceptance thresholds (support 0.9, non-foot 0.2 W, COM 1.2, slip 0.5, forward 0.05)

acceptance_for_this_probe.question: with the same controllers and the same targets, does the declared grip channel bring per-leg material slip under 0.5 while support stays above 0.9 and COM above 1.2?
acceptance_for_this_probe.decision_rule: report the numbers for grip OFF and grip ON side by side; do not tune k_grip or the cap after seeing the result
acceptance_for_this_probe.labelling: grip ON results are 'derived-channel', grip OFF results are 'frozen-body'; the two are never mixed in one claim

accounting.note: external force channel is itemised: peak force, cumulative impulse, cap hits; no force is applied when nothing is in contact
